la:noun:pensio.html:
pensĭo, ōnis, f.
pendo; lit., a weighing, weighing out; hence
,
A weight (only in Vitr.), ; .—
Transf., a paying, payment, a term of payment (class.; cf.: stipendium, pretium): pendere poenas solvere significat, ab eo, quod aere gravi cum uterentur Romani, penso eo, non numerato debitum solvebant: unde etiam pensiones dictae, Paul. ex Müll.: nihil debetur ei, nisi ex tertiā pensione,: prima,: altera tributi,. —Transf., sarcastically: etenim ista tua minime avara conjux, nimium debet diu populo Romano tertiam pensionem, i. e. her third marriage (after your death), .—
In partic.
A tax, impost (post-class.), : vectigalium,.—
Rent of a house or land (post-Aug.): aedium pensio annua,; ; .—
Interest of money (post-class.), .—
Compensation: jacturae,.

la:verb:pendo.html:
pendo, pĕpendi, pensum, 3 (pendissent, for pependissent, :
penderit for pependerit,), v. a. and n.
etym. dub.; cf. root σφαδ-, σφενδόνη, a sling; Lat. funda
.—Lit., to cause to hang down, to suspend; esp. of scales in weighing.
Act., to weigh, weigh out.
Lit. (very rare: syn. penso, expendo): unumquodque verbum staterā aurariā pendere, Varr. ap. : da pensam lanam, Titin. ap. ; , read repensum: aere gravi cum uterentur Romani, penso eo, non numerato debitum solvebant, Fest. s. v. pendere, p. 208 Müll.: pensas examinat herbas,.—
Transf., to pay, pay out (because, in the earliest times, payments were made by weighing out the metals; v.in the preced. the passage from Fest.; class.): militis stipendia ideo, quod eam stipem pendebant, Müll.: Achaei ingentem pecuniam pendunt L. Pisoni quotannis,; : vectigal populo Romano,: vectigal,: tributum pro navibus,: pretium,: coria boum in usus militares,: mercedem alicui,.—Absol.: pro pabulo pendunt,pay,.—Impers. pass.: iterumque imperii nostri publicanis penditur,.—As punishments consisted of fines in money or cattle: pendere poenas, supplicia, etc., signified to pay, suffer, undergo a penalty: pendere poenas solvere significat, Müll.: Syrus mihi tergo poenas pendet,: maximas poenas pendo temeritatis meae,: satis pro temeritate unius hominis suppliciorum pensum esse,: capitis poenas,: poenas violatae religionis sanguine et caedibus,: magna supplicia perfidiae,: crimen, culpam,.—Rarely in this signif. absol., to suffer any thing (poet.): tuis nam pendit in arvis Delius,.—
Trop.
To weigh mentally, to ponder, consider, deliberate upon, decide (class.; syn.: pensito, trutinor): vos eam (rem) suo, non nominis pondere penditote,: in philosophiā res spectatur, non verba penduntur,: causam ex veritate,: rem levi conjecturā,.—
To value, esteem, regard a thing; with gen. of the value (mostly ante-class. and poet.): neque cum me magni pendere visum'st,: aliquem,: quem tu vidisse beatus Non magni pendis,: nec jam religio divum neque numina magni Pendebantur,: unice unum plurimi pendit,: te volturium vocant: Hostisne an civis comedis, parvi pendere,: nequam hominis ego parvi pendo gratiam,lightly esteem,; so, parvi,; ; : minoris pendo tergum illorum, quam meum,care less for,: aliquem minoris,: aliquem nihili,: nihili,; ; ; cf.: non flocci pendere,: sese experturum, quanti sese penderem,: tu illum numquam ostendisti quanti penderes,.—
(Acc. to A. 2.) To pay, render (poet.): dignas pendere grates,.—
Neutr., to weigh (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): tantundem pendere par est,: talentum ne minus pondo octoginta Romanis ponderibus pendat,; ; , § 93; ; (in , read pendent).—Hence, pensus, a, um, P. a., lit. weighed; hence, trop., esteemed, valued, prized, dear (as P. a. not in Cic. or Cæs.): utra condicio pensior, Virginemne an viduam habere?: ut nihil quicquam esset carius pensiusque nobis quam nosmetipsi, Taurus ap. .—Esp., as subst.: pensum, i, n., something weighed.
Weight, consideration, scruple, importance, only in gen. sing.: nihil pensi habere aliquid, to lay no weight or stress upon a thing, to attach no value to, be indifferent to, care nothing about: sua parvi pendere, aliena cupere, ... nihil pensi neque moderati habere,: nihil pensi neque sancti habere,: neque id quibus modis assequeretur, quicquam pensi habebat,: prorsus neque dicere, neque facere quicquam pensi habebat,: nihil pensi habuit, quin, etc.,; : ut neque fas neque fidem pensi haberet,: aliquid ratum pensumque habere, Att. Capitol. ap. . —So, non pensi ducere (very rare), .—Also, non adest or est alicui pensi: nec mihi adest tantillum pensi jam, quos capiam calceos, I don't care in the least, am perfectly indifferent, : sed illis nec quid dicerent, nec quid facerent, quicquam umquam pensi fuisse,they never cared at all,: quibus si quicquam pensi umquam fuisset, non ea consilia de republicā habuissent,if they had ever had regard for any considerations,. —
Prop., the wool weighed out to a slave to spin in a day; hence, a day's work in spinning, and, in gen., spinning, a spinner's task.
Lit. (mostly ante-class. and poet.): pensum facere,; : nocturna carpentes pensa puellae,: carmine quo captae dum fusis mollia pensa Devolvunt, etc.,: famulasque ad lumina longo Exercet penso,; , (4, 14), 15: castrensia,i. e. for military garments,: pensa manu ducunt,: lanificam revocas ad sua pensa manum,; ; .—Poet., a thread spun by the Fates: durae peragunt pensa sorores,: jamque in fine dies et inexorabile pensum Deficit,: mortale resolvere, to unbind his mortal thread, i. e. to make him immortal, .—
Trop., a charge, duty, office (so in Cic.; cf.: ministerium, munus, officium): pensum meum lepide accurabo,; cf.: meum confeci,: absolvere,to perform one's duty,: me ad meum munus pensumque revocabo,; : nominis familiaeque,: operis sui peragere,.—Hence, adv.: pensē, carefully, considerately (post-class.): pensius, Flav. ap. .
la:verb:pendo.inflection: pĕpendi, pensum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:verb:pendeo.gloss: to hang (down), to be suspended; hover, overhang, float
senses: to hang (down), to be suspended; hover, overhang, float
to hang about, loiter, tarry, linger
to be put in public, exposed for sale
to hang down; to be weak or without strength; sag, droop
to hang upon a person's words; listen attentively to
to be suspended, interrupted or discontinued
to be ready to fall, hang suspended
la:verb:pendeo.html:
pendĕo, pĕpendi, 2, v. n.
intr. of pendo, q. v.
,
to hang, hang down, be suspended.
Lit., constr. with ab, ex, or in and abl.; also (poet.), with abl. alone, or with de: pendent peniculamenta, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 363 Vahl.): in candelabro pendet strigilis, Varr. ap. : in arbore,: sagittae pende, bant ab umero,, § 74: ex arbore,, § 66: ubera circum (pueri),: horrida pendebant molles super ora capilli,: capiti patiar sacros pendere corymbos, (3, 28, 39): telum ... summo clipei nequiquam umbone pependit,: deque viri collo dulce pependit onus,.—Of garments: chlamydemque ut pendeat apte, Collocat,: tigridis exuviae per dorsum a vertice pendent,.—Of slaves, who were strung up to be flogged, : quando pendes per pedes,: ibi pendentem ferit,; ; cf. : quid me fiet nunciam? Theo. Verberibus caedere pendens, : ego plectar pendens, nisi, etc.,; .—Poet., of suspended votive offerings: omnibus heu portis pendent mea noxia vota, (24): pendebatque vagi pastoris in arbore votum,: pendebit fistula pinu,: multaque praeterea sacris in postibus arma, Captivi pendent currus, etc.,.—Of one who hangs himself, : e trabe sublimi triste pependit onus,: pendentem volo Zoilum videre,.—Of any thing hung up for public notice; of the names of persons accused,, ; of goods hung up, exposed for sale,; transf., of a debtor whose goods are exposed for sale,—Prov.: pendere filo or tenui filo, to hang by a thread, i. e. to be in great danger: hac noctu filo pendebit Etruria tota, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 153 Vahl.): omnia sunt hominum tenui pendentia filo,; .—
Transf. (mostly poet.; cf. immineo).
To hang in the air, be suspended, to float, hover, overhang: per speluncas saxis structas asperis, pendentibus, Poët. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 245 Rib.); imitated,: hinc scopulus raucis pendet adesus aquis,: dum siccā tellure licet, dum nubila pendent,: hi summo in fluctu pendent,: illisaque prora pependit,; : dumosā pendere procul de rupe videbo (capros),: pendentes rupe capellae,.—So of birds, which float or hover in the air: olor niveis pendebat in aëra pennis,; : et supra vatem multa pependit avis,.— Of a rapid course: raraque non fracto vestigia pulvere pendent,.—
To hang loosely together, be unstable, movable: opertum (litus) pendeat algā,.—
To hang about, loiter, tarry, linger anywhere: nostroque in limine pendes,.—
To hang down, be flabby or flaccid, weak, without strength: fluidos pendere lacertos,: pendentesque genas et aniles aspice rugas,.—
To weigh: offula cum duabus costis quae penderet III. et XX. pondo,: cyathus pendet drachmas X., mna pendet drachmas Atticas centum,: Lucio Titio modios centum, qui singuli pondo centum pendeant, heres dato,.—
Trop.
To hang, rest, or depend upon a person or thing (class.); constr. with ex, in, ab, the simple abl., or de: tuorum, qui ex te pendent,: spes pendet ex fortunā,: ex quo verbo tota causa pendebat,; : hinc omnis pendet Lucilius,: an ignoratis. vectigalia perlevi saepe momento fortunae pendere?: salus nostra, quae spe exiguā extremāque pendet,: tam levi momento mea apud vos fama pendet,: pendere ex alterius vultu ac nutu,: oblite, tuā nostram pendere salutem,: in sententiis

omnium civium famam nostram fortunamque pendere, : ex ancipiti temporum mutatione pendere,; : deque tuis pendentia Dardana fatis,; : tyrannus, cum quo fatum pendebat amici,.—

To hang upon a person's words, to gaze fixedly, listen attentively to (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. haereo): (Dido) pendet iterum narrantis ab ore,: narrantis conjux pendet ab ore viri,: ab imagine pendet,; cf. : pervigil Arcadio Tiphys pendebat ab astro,: attentus et pendens,: ex vultu dicentis pendent omnium vultus,.—Poet., with a terminal clause: e summo pendent cupida agmina vallo, Noscere quisque suos,.—
To be suspended, interrupted, discontinued (poet. and in post-class. prose): pendent opera interrupta,: mutui datio interdum pendet,: condictio pendet,: actio negotiorum gestorum pendeat,; : pendet jus liberorum, propter jus postliminii,.—
To hang suspended, be ready to fall: nec amicum pendentem corruere patitur,.—
To be in suspense, to be uncertain, doubiful, irresolute, perplexed (cf. haesito): animus tibi pendet?: nolo suspensam et incertam plebem Romanam obscurā spe et caecā exspectatione pendere,: ne diutius pendeas,: quia quam diu futurum hoc sit, non nimis pendeo,: mortales pavidis cum pendent mentibus,.—Esp. freq.: pendere animi (locative case, v. Kühnast,): Clitipho cum spe pendebit animi,: exanimatus pendet animi,: pendeo animi exspectatione Corfiniensi,: animi pendeo et de te et de me,.—With rel.-clause: ego animi pendeo, quid illud sit negotii,: ostendis te pendere animi, quamnam rationem, etc.,; .—Less freq.: pendere animo: atque animo noctu pendens eventa timebat, Cic. poët. ap. .—In plur.: animis: quodsi exspectando et desiderando pendemus animis, cruciamur, angimur,: sollicitis ac pendentibus animis, dub. (al. animi, v. Drak. ad loc.).—With cum: plebs innumera mentibus cum dimicationum curulium eventu pendentem,.—Law t. t., to be undetermined, to await decision: pendente condicione,; ; .—
To have weight or value: bona vera idem pendent, (Haas; al. pendunt).—Hence, pendens, entis, P. a.
Hanging; in econom. lang., of fruits not yet plucked or gathered: vinum,: vindemia,: olea,: fructus,. —
Pending; hence, in jurid, Lat., in pendenti esse, to be pending, undecided, uncertain: quando in pendenti est, an, etc.,: in pendenti est posterior solutio ac prior,; : in pendenti habere aliquid,to regard a thing as uncertain, doubtful,

la:noun:penis.html:
pēnis, is, m. (abl. peni, Naev. ap. Müll.) [τὸ πέος],
a tail.
In gen. (ante-class.): caudam antiqui penem vocabant,: ... lares ludentes peni pinxit bubulo, Naev. ap. Müll.—
In partic., = membrum virile, the penis; also, by meton., for lust (class.): hodie penis est in obscenis,: ganeo, manu, ventre, pene bona patria laceraverat,; ; ; .—In a paron. with paene, .

la:prep:penes.gloss: under the command of; in the possession of
senses: under the command of; in the possession of
at the disposal or custody of
at, with, in the presence or power of, in the house of
la:prep:penes.html:
pĕnĕs, prep. with acc. [from the root pa- of pasco, v. Penates],
with, in the possession or power of; connected only with names of persons, and freq. foll. its case (class.).
Chiefly to denote possession: virtus omnia in se habet; omnia assunt bona, quem penes est virtus,; ; cf. : agri, quorum penes Cn. Pompeium omne judicium et potestas debet esse,; cf.: penes quem est potestas,: eloquentia non modo eos ornat, penes quos est, sed, etc.,; : quod penes eos summam victoriae constare intellegebant,; : si volet usus, Quem penes arbitrium est et jus et norma loquendi,: me penes est

unum vasti custodia mundi, . —So, penes se esse, have control of one's self (ἐν ἑαυτῷ εἶναι): penes te es? (for which: apud se esse,).—

Transf., with, in, in the presence or power of, in the house of, without the notion of possession: sine dote, cum ejus rem penes me habeam domi,: thesaurum tuum Me esse penes,; ; : isthaec jam penes vos psaltria'st?: hi (servi) centum dies penes accusatorem cum fuissent,; : si penes servum tabulae fuerint,: penes regem, noli velle videri sapiens,: mentis causa malae est penes te,.—Rarely with an abstract object: plures ejus rei causas afferebat, potissimam penes incuriam virorum feminarumque, the principal (cause) consisted in the indifference, etc., .

la:adj:penitus.html:
pĕnĭtus, a, um, adj.
root pa- of pasco; v. penates
,
inward, inner, interior (ante- and post-class.): exscrea usque ex penitis faucibus,: scaturigo fontis,: mente penitā conditum,, p. 259, 38.—Comp. penitior pars domūs, App. Fragm. ap. P.—Sup.: advecta ex Arabiā penitissimā,; so : in latebras abscondas pectore penitissimo,: Scythae illi penitissimi,the most remote,: de Graecorum penitissimis litteris,. —As subst.: pĕnĭta, ōrum, n., the inmost parts: mundi,: terrae,: sacri loci,.—Hence, adv., in two forms.
pĕnĭtē (poet. and post-class.), inwardly, internally, .—Sup.: penitissime,.—
pĕnĭtus (class.), inwardly, internally, in the inside (cf.: prorsus, omnino).
Lit.
In gen. (only poet.): extra penitusque coacti Exagitant venti, Sev. Aetn. 317: penitusque deus, non fronte notandus,.—
In partic., deeply, far within, into the inmost part (class.): saxum penitus excisum,: argentum penitus abditum,: jacent penitus defossa talenta,: penitus convalle virenti,: penitus terrae defigitur arbos,: penitus penetrare,: Suevos penitus ad extremos fines se recepisse,: penitus in Thraciam se abdidit,: mare retibus penitus scrutare,.—
Trop., deeply, far within. from the innermost depths or recesses: penitus ex intimā philosophiā hauriendam juris disciplinam putas,from the very depths of philosophy,: opinio tam penitus insita,so deeply rooted,: bene penitus sese dare in familiaritatem alicujus,: periculum penitus in venis et visceribus rei publicae,in the very heart,: demittere se penitus in causam,.—
Transf. (qs. through and through, to the bottom of a thing, i. e.), thoroughly, completely, wholly,

entirely, utterly (class.): caput et supercilia penitus abrasa,: utrum hic confirmasse videtur religionem an penitus totam sustulisse?: res penitus perspectae,: penitus pernoscere omnes animorum motus,: quod in memoriā meā penitus insederit,: intellegere aliquid,: amittere hanc consuetudinem et disciplinam,: diffidere rei publicae,: perdere se ipsos,: te penitus rogo ne, etc., Q. Cic. ap. : penitus toto divisos orbe Britannos,: dilecta penitus,.— Hence, to strengthen the comp.: penitus crudelior,far more,.—To strengthen the sup.: vir penitus Romano nomini infestissimus,.

la:noun:penus.html:
pĕnus, ūs and i, m. and f., also pĕ-num, i, and pĕnus, ŏris, n. (
gen. peneris, peniteris, only acc. to ; a collat. form pĕnu, Afran., acc. to P.; cf. also Don. ) [from the root pa- of pasco; Gr. πατέομαι; v. penates].
Store or provision of food provisions, victuals: est enim omne, quo vescuntur homines, penus,; cf. other and different explanations in , and tit.: De penu legatā,: annuus,; : omne penus,: ut sibi penum aliud ornet,: condus promus sum, procurator peni,: magna penus, Lucil. ap. : vinum penumque omnem,: in penum erile, Afran. ap. P.: aliquem penore privare, Auct. ap. : portet frumenta penusque,: ne situ penora mucorem contrahant,: cum ea res innoxia penora conservet,fin.: avium cujusque generis multiplex penus,: in locuplete penu,.—
The innermost part of a temple of Vesta, the sanctuary: penus vocatur locus intimus in aede Vestae, Müll.; cf.

: in penum Vestae, quod, etc., irrupit,.

la:noun:penates.gloss: Roman guardian deities of the household
senses: Roman guardian deities of the household
la:noun:penates.html:
Pĕnātes, ĭum (Penatis singulariter Labeo Antistius posse dici putat, quia pluraliter Penates dicuntur, cum patiatur proportio etiam Penas dici, ut optimas, primas, Antias, Müll. But the singular is never used; and for ΔΕΝΑΣ = ΠΕΝΑΣ, which some assume in Dion. Hal. 1, 68, it is probably most correct to read ΔΙΣ ΜΑΓΝΙΣ, v. Ambrosch, Studien und Andeut. vol. i. p. 231 sq.—
Acc. plur. PENATEIS, perh. Tab. Bant. lin. 22), m.
from the root pa, whence pascor, pabulum, pānis; also penus, and, through the notion of a storehouse or inner chamber, also penes, penetro; v. ; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, p. 425 sq.
.
Lit., the Penates, old Latin guardian deities of the household, and of the state formed of a union of households, whose seat was originally in Lavinium; usually connected with di: IN VELIA APVD AEDEM DEVM PENATIVM, Inscr. Müll.; cf.: aedes deorum Penatium in Veliā,: AEDEM DEVM PENATIVM IN VELIA, Monum. Ancyr.: di Penates,: in mensā Penatium deorum, Naev. ap. Prob. : sanctis Penatium deorum Larumque familiarium sedibus,; : MENS. IANVAR. SACRIFICANT. DIS. PENATIBVS, Calend. Farnes. ap. : v. s. ; cf. and 1678: DIIS. DEABVS PENATIBVS FAMILIARIBVS ET IOVI CETERISQVE DIIBVS,.—Without di: vos Penates patriique dii,: Ilium in Italiam portans victosque Penatis,; : impudens liqui patrios Penatis,: hostia Mollivit aversos Penates,: iniqui,: profugos posuistis Penates,; ; : IVNIANI,; cf., respecting the Penates,; Varr. and Nigid. ap. ; ; and 325.—
Transf., a dwelling, home, hearth (cf. Lares, II.): Quintius a suis dis penatibus praeceps ejectus,; : nostris succede penatibus hospes,: ferro Libycos populare penates,: conducti penates,: sub uno tecto esse atque ad eosdem penates,.—Hence, poet., of the hearth: flammis adolere penatis,.— Also, of the cells of bees, ; of the temple of a god, .

la:verb:penetro.html:
pĕnē^tro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
root pa- of pasco; v. penates
.
Act.
To put, place, or set any thing into any thing (ante- and post-class.; v. Brix ad ).
Lit.: penetrare pedem intra aedes,; : quo illic homo foras se penetrat ex aedibus? to betake one's self, go in any direction, : me ad pluris penetravi, v. 14: se in fugam,to take to flight,: in eam (specum) me penetro et recondo,.—To enter, penetrate: ea intra pectus se penetravit potio,.—In the same sense, mid.: quae penetrata queunt sensum progignere acerbum,having entered, having penetrated,; .—
Trop.: Labeo Antistius in grammaticam sese atque dialecticam litterasque antiquiores altioresque penetraverat,had penetrated into,.—
Aliquid, to pierce into any thing; to enter, penetrate any thing (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit., : (semen) penetrare locos nequit,: vox aures penetrat,: hominem cum vini vis penetravit Acris,: Illyricos sinus,: nave Aegyptum,: mediae cryptam Suburrae,. —Pass.: ut (India) penitus nequeat penetrari,: penetratae cum victoriā Media, Albania, etc.,: penetrata limina montis,: iter L. Lucullo penetratum,.—
Trop.: id Tiberii animum altius penetravit,; cf. .—With subject-clause: tum penetrabat eos, posse haec, etc.,it entered their thoughts, it occurred to them,.—
Neutr., to enter, penetrate into any place or thing, betake one's self (class.; cf.: pervado, permano).
Lit.: in palaestram,: sub terras,: ad os Pelusii,: in ipsum portum,: in castra hostium,: in artissimas fauces,: ad urbes,: per angustias,: intra vallum,: in urbem,: cum eo penetrasset,thus far,: astra per caelum penetrantia,: penetrat vox ad aures,: usque ad nares,.—Impers. pass.: in eam speluncam penetratum cum signis est,.—
Trop.: Romuli animus haec ipsa in templa penetravit,: hominum ratio in caelum usque penetravit,: nulla res magis penetrat in animos,: penetrare ad sensum judicis opinionemque,: quo non ars penetrat?: in provincias quoque grammatica penetraverat,.

la:adj:penetralis.html:
pĕnē^trālis, e, adj.
penetro
.
Piercing, penetrating (ante-class.): frigus,: ignis,: fulmineus multo penetralior ignis,.—
Transf., inward, inner, internal, interior, innermost (mostly poet.): tecta,: aeternumque adytis effert penetralibus ignem,: abditi ac penetrales foci,: di Penates ... ab eo, quod penitus insideret: ex quo etiam penetrales a poëtis vocantur,; so, per penetrales deos,; : penetrale sacrificium dicitur, quod interiore parte sacrarii conficitur: unde et penetralia cujusque dicuntur; et penes nos, quod in potestate nostrā est, Müll.—As subst.: pĕnē^trāle, is (pĕnē^tral, ; ), n.; usually in plur.: pĕnē^trālĭa, ium, the inner part, interior of any thing, esp. of a building; the inside space, an inner room (mostly poet.; not in Cic. or Cæs.; cf. adytum).
Lit.
In gen.: penetrale urbis,: in ipsis penetralibus (Britanniae),: apparent Priami et veterum penetralia regum,the inner chambers,: in penetralibus regum ipsorum,; so, penetralia alta medio tecti,: magni amnis penetralia,; .—
In partic.
A sanctuary, esp. that of the Penates, a chapel: penetralia sunt penatium deorum sacraria, Müll.: Capitolini Tonantis,.—
Transf., poet., the Penates, guardian deities: huc vittas castumque refer penetrale parentum,: avi penetralia Turni,.—
Trop., an inner place, secret place, a secret (post-Aug.), : loci aperire penetralia,: auxilia ex ipsis sapientiae penetralibus petere,: animus secedit in loca pura ... Haec eloquentiae penetralia,: penetralia animi,: mentis,.—With esp. reference to the signif. sanctuary (v. supra, I. B.): ut tantum intra suum penetral existimes adorandam (philosophiam),: sanctum penetral animi tui nesciunt,. —Adv.: pĕnē^trālĭter, inwardly, internally (post-class.), Ven. Vit. S. .

la:adj:pennus.html:
pennus, a, um, adj.
pinna
,
pointed, sharp: pennum antiqui acutum dicebant: unde et avium pennae, quia acutae, dub. (al. pinnum).

la:noun:penna.html:
penna or pinna (old forms, pesna, petna, Müll.), f.
orig. different words, penna for petna; root petor pat-; Sanscr. patāmi, to fly; Gr. πέτομαι, prop. a wing: pinna for pitna; cf. Sanscr. pitu; Gr. πίτυς, the pine-tree; Lat. pinus; cf.: spiculum, spina; prop. a sharp point or end. To a late period an effort was made to distinguish them: nec miretur (puer), cur ... fiat a pinno quod est acutum, securis utrimque habens aciem bipennis, ne illorum sequatur errorem, qui, quia a pennis duabus hoc esse nomen existimant, pennas avium dici volunt, Halm: pinnum enim antiqui acutum dicebant, dub. (v. 1. pennus): pinnas murorum, pennas avium dicimus, Flav. Cap. p. 2243 P. This dictum of the old grammar we have to retain, although the distinction is neither etymologically sound nor is it always practically true; cf. bipennis, Bramb. Lat. Orthog. p. 118. In MSS. and edd. the two forms have mostly been used indiscriminately in all meanings except II. D. E. F. infra, in which pinna only is found; cf. esp. Wagn. Orth. ; Rib. prol. ; Corss. Ausspr. 2, p. 270 sq.
,
a feather on the body of a winged creature (syn. pluma).
Lit.
Form penna: sine pennis volare haud facile est: meae alae pennas non habent,: pennarum tuarum nitor,: maduere graves aspergine pennae,.—
Form pinna: (aves) pullos pinnis fovent,: pinnarum caules omnium cavi,; : ova parire solet genus pinnis condecoratum, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 10 Vahl.): conveniebat corvos ex albis album pinnis jactare colorem, Munro: galli salaces, frequentibus pinnis,; : nam his rebus plumam pinnasque emundant,: ut statim per somnum hianti pinna in os inderetur,.—
Transf.
In plur.: pennae (pinnae), a wing (syn. ala).
Form pennae: age tu, sis, sine pennis vola,: quatere in aëre,: pennis resumptis,: vertere,to fly away, (3, 19, 6): penna, collect. for the wings, .—
Form pinnae: geminis secat aëra pinnis, (282): pinnas explicare,: o Fides alma, apta pinnis, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 410 Vahl.): densis ales pinnis obnixa, id. ap. Prob. ad (Ann. v. 148 ib.): (aquila) praepetibus pinnis (B. and K.; al. pennis), Cic. poët. Div. 1, 47, 106. —Of bees: pinnis coruscant,. —Of locusts: pinnarum stridor,.—Of gnats: pinnae culicis,.—Prov.: pinnas incidere alicui, to clip one's wings, i. e. to deprive one of power or rank, ; so, decisis humilis pinnis, with clipped wings, i. e. with disappointed hopes, ; cf. the opp.: extendere pinnas, to spread out one's wings, i. e. to attempt great things, .—
Poet., a flying, flight.
Form penna: felicibus edita pennis, i. e. with a happy omen from the flight of birds, (4, 9), 11; ; .—
Form pinna: pinnā veras dare notas,.—
A feather on an arrow (poet.).
Form penna: per jugulum pennis tenus acta sagitta est,.—Hence,
Meton., an arrow (poet.).
Form penna: cervos pennā petere,.—
Form pinna: olor trajectus pinnā,.—
In late Lat., a pen.—Form penna: instrumenta scribae, calamus et penna: sed calamus arboris est, penna avis,.—
A fin. —Form pinna, .—
A pinnacle.—Form pinna: turres contabulantur, pinnae loricaeque ex cratibus attexuntur,; : milites Metelli ... a pinnis hostis defendebant facillime funditore, Quadrig. ap. ; : templi,.—
In mechanics.
A float or bucket of a water-wheel.—Form pinna, . —
A stop or key of a water-organ.— Form pinna,.

la:noun:Pentheus.html:
Pentheus, ĕi and ĕos, m., = Πενθεύς,
son of Echion and Agave, grandson of Cadmus, and king of Thebes; having treated with contempt the rites of Bacchus, he was torn in pieces by his mother and her sisters when under the influence of the god, ; (4, 16), 24; 3 (4), 22, 33; ; ; .—Hence,
Penthēĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Pentheus, Penthean: mater,.—
Penthēus, a, um, adj., = Πενθεῖος, of or belonging to Pentheus, Penthean, .—
Penthīdes, ae, m., = Πενθείδης, a male descendant of Pentheus, and 609.

la:noun:penuria.html:
pēnūrĭa or paenūrĭa, ae, f.
Gr. πένομαι, to toil; πένης, poor; cf. σπάνις, πεῖνα
,
want, need, scarcity of any thing (class.; syn.: inopia, egestas).
Lit., esp. of want of the necessaries of life; constr. with or (less freq.) without a gen.: cibi,: victūs,: edendi,: aquarum,: rerum necessariarum,: frumenti,. —Absol.: neque enim est umquam penuria parvi,he is never in want who requires but little,: penuriam temporum sustinere,to supply their temporary wants,: in penuriā,in time of scarcity,: afflixit te penuriā,; .—Of want of other things: civium,: magna sapientium civium bonorumque penuria,: cujus generis (amicorum) est magna penuria,: liberorum,: mulierum,: agri, vectigalium, pecuniae,: argenti,: arborum,.—
Trop.: consilii,: vivae vocis,.

la:verb:penso.html:
penso, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a.
pendo
,
to weigh or weigh out carefully (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; not in Cic., for in Off. 2, 19, 68, conpensandum is the correct reading. Neither is it found in Plaut., Ter., Lucr., or Cæs.; syn.: pendo, expendo).
Lit.: aurum,; ; : C. Gracchi caput auro pensatum,paid for with its weight in gold,: odores ac purpurae et auro pensanda,worth their weight in gold,.—Prov.: pensare aliquem eādem trutinā,to weigh one in the same balance, judge one by the same standard,.—
Transf.
To counterbalance with any thing, to compensate, recompense, repay, make good, requite; for the usual compensare: exiguā turis impensā tanta beneficia pensaturi,: beneficia beneficiis,; : praematuram mortem immortali nominis sui memoriā,: vulnera et sanguis aviditate praedae,; cf. ; : vicem alicujus, to supply the place of a thing, to compensate for a thing, ; transmarinae res quādam vice pensatae,: iter,to shorten the way,.—
To pay, repay, punish with any thing: nece pudorem,: omnia uno ictu,: nefarium concubitum voluntariā morte,.—
To purchase with any thing: vitam auro,: victoriam damno militis,.—
To exchange for any thing: palatia caelo,: laetitiam moerore,.—
To allay, quench: sitim,.—
To weigh, ponder, examine, consider: ex factis, non ex dictis, amicos pensare,: ad consilium pensandum temporis opus esse,; ; ; : singula animi consulta,: stat pensata diu belli sententia,.

la:adj:pennatus.html:
pennātus (pinn-), a, um, adj.
penna
,
furnished with wings, winged (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): hic Jovis altisoni subito pennata (al. pinnata) satelles, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 47, 106: apes,: serpentes,: pennati equi, quos pegasos vocant,: Zephyrus,: ferrum,an arrow,.—Subst.: pennāta, ōrum, n. (sc. animalia), winged creatures, birds: pennatorum infecunda sunt, quae aduncos habent ungues,.—Prov.: Frustra jacitur rete ante oculos pennatorum,.—Comp.: voto pennatior, Auct. Itin. Alex. 69.—
Transf.: pennatas impennatasque agnas in Saliari carmine spicas significat cum aristis, et alias sine aristis ... (Aelius oves veteres et) agnas novas voluit intellegi, Paul. ex Müll.

la:adj:penetrabilis.html:
pĕnĕtrābĭlis, e, adj.
penetro

Pass., that can be pierced or penetrated, penetrable (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): corpus nullo penetrabile telo,: cum sit nulli penetrabilis,: pectus ferro,: terra,: caput haud penetrabile Nili,inaccessible,.—
Act., piercing, penetrating (poet. and in post-class. prose): Boreae penetrabile frigus,: telum,: harundo,: fulmen,: vinum penetrabilius in venas,: querimonia,.—Comp.: sermo Dei est penetrabilior omni gladio ancipiti,.—
= penetralis (late Lat.): ad regni penetrabilia, Laurent. Hom. 1.

la:adj:pensior.gloss: paid, suspended, weighed; that which is paid, suspended or weighed
la:adj:pensior.html:
pensĭo, ōnis, f.
pendo; lit., a weighing, weighing out; hence
,
A weight (only in Vitr.), ; .—
Transf., a paying, payment, a term of payment (class.; cf.: stipendium, pretium): pendere poenas solvere significat, ab eo, quod aere gravi cum uterentur Romani, penso eo, non numerato debitum solvebant: unde etiam pensiones dictae, Paul. ex Müll.: nihil debetur ei, nisi ex tertiā pensione,: prima,: altera tributi,. —Transf., sarcastically: etenim ista tua minime avara conjux, nimium debet diu populo Romano tertiam pensionem, i. e. her third marriage (after your death), .—
In partic.
A tax, impost (post-class.), : vectigalium,.—
